headline: Netherlands buried Tunisia's early promise with suffocating control
story: Tunisia stunned Netherlands with a third-minute goal and briefly suggested they might resist the Dutch machine. But Netherlands equalized within four minutes and thereafter imposed a possession stranglehold that Tunisia could never escape. The shape of the match was determined not by a single flash but by relentless attrition: Netherlands' high-press engine (9.7 phases to 0.8) forced Tunisia into ever-tighter defensive postures until their structure simply fractured.

The statistics exposed what happened. Netherlands' expected-goals advantage (1.79 to 0.76) barely captured their true dominance; the real gulf was ball recovery time. Netherlands regained possession in 12.6 seconds against Tunisia's 29.8—a 17-second differential meaning relentless Dutch probing while Tunisia gasped between phases. Mastouri and Mejbri fought bravely, but Van Dijk and Brobbey's press movement ensured Tunisia's 5-4-1 became a prison. The pivot was Tunisia's failure to convert a 0.17-xG chance in the second minute; going 2-0 up would have shifted the match's entire psychology.

keyMoment.text: Netherlands' second goal arrived after Tunisia's defensive structure had entirely given way to Dutch momentum.

home.verdict: Capitulated to press intensity and recovery disadvantage.
points: Ball recovery of 29.8s versus Netherlands' 12.6s guaranteed possession loss; must accelerate defensive circulation.
Missed big chance at minute 2 (xG 0.17) cost the match psychologically; clinical finishing non-negotiable.
High-press exposure (0.8 phases vs 9.7) shows defensive formation too rigid; needed proactive midfield disruption.

away.verdict: Possession and press machine overcame early shock, but defensive fragility at 7' exposed vulnerability.
points: Ball recovery efficiency at 12.6s created unending attacking platforms; this speed and discipline won decisively.
High-press phases (9.7) systematically dismantled Tunisia's defensive shape; relentless press is the foundation.
Early concession at 7' (xG 0.45) signals positioning lapses; must tighten immediate reaction to forward movement.

statLine: Netherlands recovered the ball in 12.6 seconds to Tunisia's 29.8—a 17-second chasm that transformed possession into relentless territorial dominance.
